# Collective-Intelligence @ Stage 3 — Basic Impulse

> developed 2026-07-26. Deepened from 73 to 140+ lines.

## Expression on this line

Collective-intelligence at Order 2 is **conditioned collective behavior**: the first
moment where a system's collective coordination is shaped by past experience rather than
just present stimulus. A flock of birds that has learned to avoid a particular location
will avoid it even when the danger is no longer present. A colony that has learned to
concentrate resources in one area will continue to do so even when conditions change.
This is the birth of collective memory — the system now carries a rudimentary internal
model of where effective collective coordination is likely to be.

The key advance from Stage 2 is **associative collective learning**. The organism no
longer coordinates only based on the immediate stimulus; it coordinates based on
stimuli that have been paired with significant collective outcomes in the past. This
opens up a fundamentally new possibility: the system can coordinate for conditions that
are not currently present. It can anticipate collective needs, even if no significant
stimulus is there today. This is the first step toward collective planning.

Collective preferences begin to differentiate at this stage. The organism does not
treat all collective configurations equally — it learns to prefer some over others
based on conditioning history. This is the first collective discrimination: "this
coordination pattern works, that one doesn't."

But collective preferences at Stage 3 remain **rigid and context-free**. The conditioned
response occurs regardless of whether the context has changed.

The transition from Stage 3 to Stage 4 occurs when the organism begins to differentiate
collective behaviors by **category** rather than just by individual conditioning history.

In human development, Stage 3 corresponds to the toddler's collective behavior: "I
like group play" driven by immediate experience and basic conditioning.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** The first rudiments of social collective learning emerge. Young animals
  observe which coordination patterns their mothers use and imitate.

- **UR:** The individual organism exhibits conditioned collective preferences. It
  reliably approaches preferred collective configurations and avoids conditioned
  collective aversions.

- **LL:** Simple social collective coordination emerges. Flocking behavior represents
  collective intelligence at Stage 3.

- **LR:** The organism's learned associations are the institutional structure of
  Stage 3 collective intelligence.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Compulsive repetition of conditioned collective behavior even
  when it no longer leads to effective coordination.

- **Dark allergy:** Failure to form conditioned collective associations.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to conditioned collective preferences beyond their
  useful life.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejection of conditioned collective preferences themselves.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Conditioned collective behavior:** The system's collective behavior is shaped by
  past associations, not just present stimuli.

- **Rigid preference structure:** Collective preferences are fixed and context-free.

- **No collective categorization:** Collective configurations are experienced as
  individual items, not categories of coordination.

- **No perspective-taking:** The system cannot imagine how collective behavior looks
  from another vantage point.
